title: Why the show closed in Danzig
summary: Wooding says Goldberg persuaded the Polish backer Sirotq to cut salaries, so the show broke up at Danzig.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. And I want to hear about the closing of the show, and why, and what happened to you.

Well, we closed in -- we had a reason for closing. Because, again, the work of Goldberg. Cause we was all tired of it anyhow. We had money and we was all tired of the show. But Goldberg showed -- Leonidow was backed out now. Was -- Sirotq, Sirotq. And Plaskoff was his secretary. Plaskoff was -- both of them were Polish people, you see. And Plaskoff tried to keep the thing together, but Goldberg influenced Sirotq that, 'Look, you're paying these people too much money. And we can get cheaper talent around here. And they'll do the same thing, because they're all the same.' You know what I mean? And that was actually what it was, you see? And he --

And he showed him wherein -- but people -- so when we reached Danzig was where the show didn't go any farther. And they closed the show, but Goldberg was forcing the show to close, because that would mean that he would get a better job and have more money, too. But the show would be less. And for his duty of getting these people cheap, he would naturally raise his own salary. Better to put up one man's salary and cut all the other people.
